subject: Questions about uptime/latency measurement & temporary SLA carve-out
content:
From: Danielle Morris <danielle.morris@acme-corp.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Cc: procure@acme-corp.com, cloudops@acme-corp.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Procurement questionnaire: uptime/latency measurement + carve-out request

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the call yesterday. Procurement asked us to send a short questionnaire that covers how Redwood measures uptime and latency, how alerts are generated, and what access we get to metrics/dashboards. Two specific asks from legal/procurement:

- Confirm the precise definition and calculation for "uptime" (including boundary conditions for client-side errors vs. server-side).
- Explain how latency SLOs (p95/p99) are computed (aggregation window, whether outliers are trimmed, and sampling implications).

Separately: because this is a pilot, our CloudOps team wants to request a temporary SLA carve-out (30–60 days) during initial integration to allow rolling restarts and model tuning without penalty. Please provide the process and approval path for an exception; procurement wants to capture this in the contract appendix.

I've attached the procurement questionnaire and included CloudOps on the thread.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — we need an answer by end of week to keep the procurement timeline.

Best,
Danielle
Director, Cloud Platform
Acme Corp

--- Attachment: procurement-questionnaire.pdf (16KB)

------------------------------------------------------------

From: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
To: Danielle Morris <danielle.morris@acme-corp.com>
Cc: procure@acme-corp.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire: uptime/latency measurement + carve-out request

Hi Danielle — thanks for sending this over. Below is a concise packet of answers and the temporary carve-out process. I'm attaching a zip with more detailed evidence and our standard measurement spec.

High-level answers (short version):

1) Uptime (Availability) definition
- Numerator: successful inference responses returned by Redwood's inference gateway (HTTP 2xx/3xx).
- Denominator: total inference requests reaching the gateway (excludes malformed client requests that are rejected with 4xx at the client validation layer — these are classified separately).
- Resolution: 1-minute buckets aggregated to daily and monthly rollups. Monthly availability = 1 - (sum(failed_requests)/sum(total_requests)) over the month.
- Failure modes counted: 5xx responses from runtime, request timeouts at the gateway, and explicit "model-unavailable" rejections. Network errors between customer edge and our public ingress are not counted as Redwood failures unless they reach our gateway.

2) Latency SLOs (p95/p99 computation)
- We measure end-to-end server-side tail latencies at the gateway egress point (time from request received by gateway to final byte sent from runtime).
- Percentiles: computed on 1-minute windows using t-digest aggregation, then aggregated to daily/monthly percentiles using weighted merging (preserves tail behavior).
- Outliers: we do not trim by default; we flag known maintenance windows or injected load as exceptions when an approved carve-out is active.
- Sampling: all production requests are collected; when traffic exceeds collection limits we apply deterministic reservoir sampling with a conservatively large sample (we record the sampler seed and sample_rate in telemetry).

3) Monitoring & Alerts
- Default alerting: PagerDuty triggers for availability drops > 0.5% inside a 5-minute window or sustained p99 increases > 2x baseline for 15 minutes.
- Dashboards: read-only Grafana links can be shared; dashboards include request rate, error breakdown, latency histograms, and service runbook links.
- Access: customers get read-only Grafana access (RBAC) and can request short-lived API keys for metric pulls under a limited contract clause.

4) Evidence & retention
- Telemetry retention: raw minute-level aggregates retained 13 months; full traces and per-request logs retained 30 days by default (longer retention available as an add-on).
- Evidence: we provide a monthly SLO packet (raw aggregates + percentile calculations + runbook summary) as part of procurement onboarding.

Temporary SLA carve-out process (for pilots/integration)
- Scope: carve-outs cover specified windows/hosts or maintenance activities and are time bounded (max 90 days).
- Request: customer raises a "slo-exception" request via support@redwood.com with dates, affected model/route, and justification.
- Approval: Director of Sales + Technical Program Manager sign-off for pilot carve-outs <= 60 days; >60 days require VP approval.
- Audit: carve-outs are logged and an evidence packet showing excluded windows is added to the monthly SLO packet.

Attachments I've included: the detailed measurement spec + a short runbook excerpt. Also linking a read-only Grafana invite in a follow-up note.

Next steps: we can either (a) approve a 45-day temporary carve-out for your pilot (if you confirm dates and scope), or (b) run the integration under standard SLOs with a documented maintenance window. Which would you prefer?

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: CloudOps <cloudops@acme-corp.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Cc: procure@acme-corp.com, danielle.morris@acme-corp.com
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire: uptime/latency measurement + carve-out request

Thanks, Tessa. A couple of clarifying questions from our SRE team:

- When you say "gateway egress point", can you confirm whether the latency measurement includes model decode time when using streaming responses (we have streaming use-cases)?
- For reservoir sampling: what's the maximum sample rate you might apply at peak (we need to know whether p99 is reliable for low-traffic endpoints)?

Also, for the carve-out approval process: what is the expected minimum lead time for an approved carve-out and do we get a notification when the carve-out is active/ended?

—Jordan, CloudOps (on behalf of the SRE team)

------------------------------------------------------------

From: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
To: cloudops@acme-corp.com, danielle.morris@acme-corp.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 10:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire: uptime/latency measurement + carve-out request

Hi Jordan — great questions. Quick answers below and more detail in the attached runbook excerpt.

- Streaming: we measure decode time as part of the server-side end-to-end latency for streaming responses. For streaming endpoints we report both total request completion percentiles and an "initial-response" latency (time to first byte) to isolate model generation startup time.
- Reservoir sampling: at extreme peaks we reserve up to 5% of requests for deterministic sampling; in practice for API customers the sample rate is typically 10% only under extremely high QPS (>100k qps across a shard) and otherwise we capture >90% of request events. We publish the sample rate with each aggregate window so you can decide whether to accept the percentile numbers for low-volume routes.
- Carve-out lead time & notifications: we ask for a 48-hour lead time for scheduled carve-outs; emergency carve-outs can be requested and are triaged within 4 business hours. We will send start/end notifications to the listed contacts and an audit entry to the contract appendix.

Karthik: can you confirm whether we should include a pre-approved 45-day carve-out clause for pilot customers by default, or keep it one-off per request?

Thanks,
Tessa

Danielle — looping back with the official packet and next steps. Per internal approvals, Redwood can offer a 45-day pre-approved carve-out for the pilot. To proceed we need:

1) Confirmation of the exact date range you want excluded (start/end).
2) The list of model routes or project IDs (you already shared these; confirm final list).
3) Primary contact for carve-out notifications (email + pager if you want PD alerts).

We attached the full evidence package and a short contract clause draft that Ben prepared. Also included is a read-only Grafana invite link (text file with URL) so your SREs can validate percentiles during the integration.

If you confirm the three items above, Sales will annotate the deal and Legal/Procurement can include the appendix in the contract. Happy to jump on a quick call to finalize.

Thanks,
